data.hypothesis: The best reported T1 candidate is the 8x32 output tile at K-depth 16 (19.5267 ms). Increasing only its row tile to 16 while retaining 32 coalesced columns and K-depth 16 tests whether greater B-tile reuse and fewer CTAs outweigh twice as many threads per CTA and greater A staging. The 16x32, K-depth-32 candidate measured 22.8994 ms, so this is a distinct tile-shape experiment, not an assumed speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use this as a focused comparison for the proposed 16x32, K-depth-16 tile; it does not establish that changing tile height alone causes the timing difference.
memory_lessons.claim: The reported 8x32 output tile at K-depth 16 was valid and averaged 0.0195267 s; the reported 16x32 output tile at K-depth 32 was valid and averaged 0.0228994 s.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a 16x32 output tile at K-depth 16 with the same correctness and repeated-timing protocol.

memory_lessons.applicability: The coalesced control is a useful comparison for the objective's initial lane-mapping change, but its timing does not isolate the effect of shared-memory tiling.
memory_lessons.claim: The coalesced one-output-per-thread control was correct and averaged 0.0234084 s; the supplied baseline was correct and averaged 0.2734839 s.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare future tile candidates against both the best valid tile result and the coalesced control.

data.notes: The candidate retains the run entry point and alpha/beta update, uses synchronous shared-memory staging with masked tails, and adds no allocations or external math-library calls. The controller must check correctness and repeated timing; no result is claimed for this proposal. No selected parent was supplied, integration_source_ids is empty, and sources_kept is therefore [].
transformations: Replaced the supplied per-output serial kernel with a 16x32-output CTA tile and K-depth-16 synchronous shared-memory staging.
Mapped threadIdx.x across 32 output columns so warp lanes access contiguous B and C columns, with one output accumulator per thread.
Masked A and B loads and C stores to support matrix tails; used size_t offsets and quotient/remainder grid calculations.
Preserved the run entry point, alpha/beta semantics, and scratch-buffer signature without adding allocations or external math-library calls.
